newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten says would take low HK tax into UK politics.
newsitem.headline: Patten says would take low HK tax into UK politics.

text.p: British governor Chris Patten said on Friday he would import Hong Kong's low public spending and taxes, and international-minded attitude, into British and European politics.
He declined to comment what he would do after his governorship ends when the British colony reverts to China at midnight on June 30 next year, however.

"I think I will go back from Hong Kong with a very strong view that public spending should form a smaller proportion of a community's income and the taxes should be lower if you want to encourage greater economic growth and greater economic dynamism," he said during a question and answer with the public about the final policy address he delivered on Wednesday.

"I take from Hong Kong the very clear view that it's possible to be an open community, it's possible to be an international-minded community while retaining a sense of identity and that's a point which perhaps has particular relevance to the debate in the United Kingdom about Britain's role in the European Community," he said.
Patten, once tipped as a possible future British prime minister, said he "might write a book one day".
There has been speculation that Patten could return to British politics or join the European Commission.
